data.gender_notes: Leonel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'leo' meaning lion and 'nuel' meaning new or little. Leonel represents a brave and powerful individual. The name Leonel carries the meaning “Lion man” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Leonel usually hope their child will grow to embody lion man and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Leonel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lion man.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Leonel total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_greek.name: Λεωνέλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Λεωνέλ προέρχεται από το ελληνικό όνομα Λέων που σημαίνει 'λέων' και το γαλλικό μικρό επίθετο 'el' που σημαίνει μικρός. Το όνομα συνδέεται με το σύμβολο του θάρρους και της ανδρείας.

in_latin.name: Leonel
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Leonel derivatur ex nomine Leonis qui est leo et filius. Nomen significat 'filium leonis' et refertur ad fortitudinem et animositatem quae sunt virtutes christianae.

in_english.name: Leonel
in_english.long_meaning: The name Leonel is derived from the Hebrew word 'lion' and the Latin suffix '-el' meaning 'of God' or 'strong'. It symbolizes courage, strength, and bravery. Historically, it was used to signify someone with lion-like qualities, embodying the Christian virtues of valor and fearlessness.

historical_references.context: A Breton saint, born in Brittany, France, who is venerated as a patron saint of Brittany and France. Leonel, the son of a Breton count, is said to have been evangelized by Saint Malo. He was a monk at the Abbey of Redon and later became the bishop of Nantes. Leonel was imprisoned in Angers by the Frankish king Childebert I and died as a martyr in prison.

historical_references.context: A Portuguese saint, who was born in Porto, Portugal, as a illegitimate son of King Sancho I. Leonel was raised as a nobleman but later joined the Dominican Order and became a priest. He was a learned theologian and a noted preacher. Saint Leonel is venerated as the patron saint of Porto and the Armed Forces.
